text:
lia: heads up — saw a user report where per-key burst credits weren't deducted on the immediate retry, and the completion tokens got counted twice after a tool call fallback :confused:

sam: repro steps?

lia: short: client got 429 from primary model, retried with same request id, request succeeded but quota shows both the failed attempt and the retry debited. also saw fallback to tool variant — tool output tokens added on top of the completion tokens from the retry.

sam: can you paste logs?

lia: pasted minimal log below:

```
2026-11-05T17:42:01Z INFO quota.check org=org_17 key=key_abc burst_available=100
2026-11-05T17:42:01Z WARN inference.call req_id=req_xyz model=redwood-xl status=429 tokens_prompt=12 tokens_completion=0 billed=false
2026-11-05T17:42:02Z INFO inference.retry req_id=req_xyz.retry1 parent=req_xyz
2026-11-05T17:42:03Z INFO inference.call req_id=req_xyz.retry1 model=redwood-xl-fallback status=200 tokens_prompt=0 tokens_completion=80 billed=true
2026-11-05T17:42:03Z INFO tokens.debit org=org_17 key=key_abc amount=80 origin=completion req_id=req_xyz.retry1
2026-11-05T17:42:03Z INFO tokens.debit org=org_17 key=key_abc amount=12 origin=prompt req_id=req_xyz
2026-11-05T17:42:03Z INFO tokens.debit org=org_17 key=key_abc amount=25 origin=tool_call req_id=req_xyz.retry1
```

lia: result: console shows 117 tokens debited but support request shows user only expected 80 (they only saw the successful response).

morgan: looks like we double-counted the prompt from the original failed call and still charged tool_call separately. why is `billed=false` not preventing the prompt debit?

ashley: probable cause: quota check and token debit are split timewise. failed call sets `billed=false` but we still log prompt tokens for metrics and later the retry's completion and the tool_call get billed without dedup. Also per-key burst allowance is decremented during `quota.check` but there's a race where the retry occurs before the grant is recorded.

ryan: I remember we switched to an eventual-write path for quota grants to reduce latency — grants are async write to rate-limiter store with 500ms window. If retry hits before the grant write completes we create a duplicate grant and double-debit.

sam: suggestions: 1) tie token debits to canonical request id (root req id) and de-duplicate by `canonical_req` tag; 2) ensure tool_call tokens are attributed to the canonical request and have a separate `origin` so dashboard can show breakdown; 3) treat `billed=false` events as non-billable unless matched to an explicit `bill_on_success` marker.

lia: agree on canonical id. current system munges ids for retries (append `.retryN`) which confuses billing pipeline.

morgan: quick fix: set dedupe TTL on tokens.debit for same canonical_req to 1s and check `retry_of` field. Long term: switch billing write to be idempotent keyed by `(org, canonical_req, origin)`.

ashley: console & telemetry asks: we need a new metric `billing.duplicate_detected` and dashboard card per-api-key showing "debited tokens vs expected tokens" with breakdown by origin (prompt/completion/tool). That'll make customer disputes easier.

ryan: for Dedicated customers with strict SLAs we should optionally enforce synchronous grant writes (config flag on pool) to avoid race windows.

sam: action items: 
- sam: add unit tests for dedupe on billing pipeline (PR incoming)
- ashley: add new telemetry event and update console card mockups
- morgan: hotfix to add 1s dedupe TTL in billing service today
- lia: collect 3 sample org traces and open support followups

quota-bot: note: quota-enforcer adjusted burst window for key=key_abc at 2026-11-05T18:00:00Z to avoid transient double-grants.

lia: sounds good. one more UX note — in rollouts we expose a "charge-preview" in the console for canary traffic so SREs can see expected debit vs actual. would help catch this during canaries.

sam: yes — make charge-preview hook into realtime telemetry stream `billing.preview` and include `dedupe_score` so we can surface risky requests.

lia: thanks everyone. I'll collect traces and put follow-up thread in incidents if we find customer-facing impact. :thumbsup:
